Last week, I had the honor of presenting the findings from our long-term study on the impact of climate change on trout populations in Yellowstone National Park. Our research, conducted over the past five years, has revealed some concerning trends that underscore the urgent need for conservation efforts.

One particularly memorable moment from our fieldwork was when we observed a significant decline in the cutthroat trout population in a stream that had historically been one of the healthiest. This decline was directly linked to rising water temperatures and reduced oxygen levels, both of which are exacerbated by climate change. It was a stark reminder of the delicate balance of aquatic ecosystems and the critical role that environmental stewardship plays in preserving them.

Our research highlights the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and community engagement. We've partnered with Yellowstone National Park, the National Fisheries Institute, and local conservation groups to develop strategies to mitigate the effects of climate change on trout populations.
